QF.id: Terminology in Equity and Debt Markets_15

question.text: A callable bond gives the right to:

answer.text: The bondholder to demand early repayment
The issuer to redeem the bond before maturity
The bondholder to convert into equity
The regulator to cancel the bond

explanation.text: The Logic: A callable bond gives the issuer (not the holder) the right to redeem (call back) the bond before its stated maturity, usually at a specified call price. The issuer typically exercises this right when prevailing interest rates fall and the bond can be refinanced at a lower coupon. The Trap: A puttable bond gives the holder the right to demand early repayment. A convertible bond allows conversion to equity. Callable is specifically the issuer's right. Note: The Series XV Research Analyst workbook's bond-types section (zero-coupon, floating-rate, convertible, principal-protected, inflation-protected, foreign-currency, external/Masala bonds) does not directly define callable bonds. Detailed callable-bond pricing/behaviour is covered more thoroughly in Series IV (Interest Rates Derivatives).
